DEFECT FIX, no new lines claimed (guns.js has only 3 free and these lines are already inside the existing covers=171 claim).

TWO defects in GunPod, both in the pod's taper:

1. THE HOUSING TAPER WAS REVERSED. src/guns.js:397 is `CylinderGeometry(0.16, 0.2, 1.5, 12)` and :396 is `body.rotation.x = Math.PI / 2`. CylinderGeometry puts radiusTop at +Y, and R_x(+90) sends (0,1,0) to (0,0,1), so the TOP (0.16) lands at +Z, which is AFT in Three's -Z-forward frame, and the BOTTOM (0.2) faces the MUZZLE. The JS pod is therefore WIDE (0.2) AT THE MUZZLE. Guns.cs had `Cylinder(BodyRRear=0.2, BodyRFront=0.16, ...)`, and ProceduralPropMesh.Cylinder(rNear, rFar, ...) puts rNear on the -Z (aft) ring and rFar on the +Z (muzzle) ring, so the Unity pod was narrow at the muzzle -- tapering the wrong way down its whole 1.5 m. The class header asserted the same wrong thing in prose ('front/muzzle end narrower at 0.16'), so comment and code agreed with each other and both disagreed with the JS; the header is rewritten with the +Y->+Z derivation spelled out. Constants renamed BodyRAft/BodyRMuzzle so the mistake cannot be re-made by reading the names.

2. THE BARREL TAPER WAS GONE. src/guns.js:399 is `CylinderGeometry(0.05, 0.055, 1.35, 10)`; Guns.cs had collapsed it to a single `BarrelR = 0.0525f`, the mean of the two. Restored as BarrelRAft=0.05 / BarrelRMuzzle=0.055 by the same aft/muzzle rule (the JS barrel really is 0.5 mm wider at the muzzle -- odd-looking, measured, and the spec).

NOT TOUCHED, confirmed correct: MuzzleLocal/MuzzleWorld (GUNPOD_MUZZLE_WORLD matches to a float32 tie on a real Transform, so the forward flip and the yaw negation are both right), PodLocalPos, the brake, the struts (box dims and the two negated z offsets), and the metal material.

WHY IT SURVIVED: nothing had ever paired GunPod. Pass4ExtrasProbe + tools/_probe_pass4extras.mjs are new, and the JS side reads the radii straight out of src/guns.js by regex and prints them as rMuzzle/rAft rather than top/bottom -- which is exactly the framing that made the reversal visible instead of arguable.

NO CHANGE TO RifleHolds.cs -- the suspected sign flip in the cover and reload branches IS NOT THERE. The defect was in the PROBE, and the broken pair is what hid it.

THE VERDICT. The hand-paired table read:
           js handX  cs handX   js handZ   cs handZ
  aim      0.18000   0.25718    -0.31280   -0.32907
  carry    0.18000   0.25182    -0.29355   -0.29410
  cover    0.12000   0.06908    -0.41244   +0.29449
  reload  -0.06190  -0.05741    -0.38468   +0.24522
The two 'flipped' modes were the CORRECT ones. weapons.js:884's `cf` is `crossVectors(_up, _right)` for cover/reload and plain `_fwd` (the aim) otherwise. RifleHolds.ChestLine ports that cross product as `Cross(right, up)` -- operands swapped -- which is right: a reflection has det -1, so R(a x b) = -(Ra x Rb), and swapping the operands is how you recover the mirrored vector. Cross(+X,+Y) = +Z = Unity forward, exactly as cross(+Y,+X) = -Z = Three forward. So cover/reload put the weapon and both hands IN FRONT of the body in both engines. Meanwhile RangeProbe.cs fed `applyRifleHold` an aim vector of `new Vector3(0f, 0f, -1f)` -- Three's forward, retyped into Unity, where it points BACKWARD. aim/carry build `cf` straight off that aim, so they came out mirrored and then 'agreed' with the JS's raw Z; cover/reload ignore the aim for `cf` and came out right and 'disagreed'. A rig difference cannot flip a sign on two of four modes while matching a third to 0.2% -- correct -- but the flip was in the modes that read the probe's bad input, not in the two that avoided it.

WHAT CHANGED (probe side only):
- Editor/Probes/RangeProbe.cs: aimFwd is now `(0,0,1)` with the handedness reasoning at the literal. The real-banana block's lines became CSONLY RIFLEHOLD_REAL/RIFLECHAINS_REAL (a standalone reach/NaN assertion with no JS counterpart, still gating the exit code). With the aim fixed, all four of its modes now sit in front of the body: aim handZ +0.26994 (was -0.32907), carry +0.23618, reload +0.24607, cover +0.29451.
- New RunRifleHoldSynth() builds the SAME synthetic rig tools/_probe_range.mjs:117-137 builds (shoulder 1.40 m, 0.27 m upper arm, 0.26 m forearm; local z offsets mirrored, X not mirrored because the gun-side arm is at +X in BOTH engines) and prints paired RIFLEHOLD/RIFLESUPPORT/RIFLECHAINS lines in the body's own frame -- R toward the gun shoulder, U up, F forward -- because F is -Z here and +Z there and a raw Z can never agree however correct the port is. Everything else these functions compute is already frame-invariant (hints are expressed in up/right/fwd; ApplyReachPose's two-bone IK has no cross product), so that projection is the whole of the conversion.
- The synthetic rig goes through a real CharacterRig, and that is faithful rather than convenient: CharacterRig's NormalizeHeight() measures 0 on a rendererless rig and skips both the scale and the sole offset, so the bones keep the exact local coordinates set; and FootPoses.RifleShoulder returns null for it (no Animator -> PoseRig.HasArms false), which is precisely what the JS's `{}` rigStub does with its missing `rifleShoulder`. So the aim/carry pocket FALLBACK is exercised on both sides, not on one.
- tools/_probe_range.mjs: the pose lines are no longer JSONLY *_SYNTH; they print the same paired keys. Its own reach/NaN gate stays JSONLY RIFLEHOLD_SYNTH_CHECK.

AUDITED AND LEFT ALONE while establishing which side was wrong: all five un-wrapped `cross(up,right)` sites (rifleChains' cf :884, BoreReach's fwd0 :1018, ApplyRifleReloadHand's pouch/onMag :1089/:1134, ApplyCoverArms' fwd :1238) are all swapped consistently; Quaternion.AngleAxis(ReloadRoll, line) needs no sign change (a mirror maps R(a,theta) to R(Ma,-theta) in right-handed algebra, and Unity's AngleAxis already IS the negative-sense convention, so the two cancel); the reload cant `up*cos - right*sin + cf*LEAN`, the cover tilt, the carry dip, the pocket fallback, `butt - gripX`, `-upA*(0.02+gripY)` and the GRIP_RAKE wrist line are all line-for-line the JS. The akm catalogue entry's own numbers check out against the JS output arithmetically: butt 0.26*1.1 = 0.286, gripX 0.012*1.1 = 0.0132, and 0.286-0.0132 = 0.2728 is exactly the JS's aim handZ of -0.04-0.2728 = -0.31280.

DEFECT FIX found while auditing defect 1's handedness, same class, one token: GunPoseBlend.Apply's no-aim fallback. src/gunanim.js:565/567 falls back to `(0,0,-1)` for the BODY-FACING frame when the caller passes no aim; that is Three's forward, so Unity's is `Vector3.forward`. Retyped verbatim it put the whole pose frame 180 degrees round (r = Cross(up,f), u = Cross(f,r), and `World()` projects every clip-space direction through them), i.e. the arms posed as if the hero faced backwards, whenever a caller passed no aim.

DELIBERATELY LEFT AS -Z in the same file: `_gunBore`/`_gunUp` (:413, :494-495) and `GunF`'s initialiser (:418). Those live in the reference CLIP's space, not the world's -- `World(d)` consumes them as `f * -d.z`, flipping the z itself -- so they are correct at -Z and flipping them would double-apply the rule (the project's own 'mirror X ONCE, not twice' gotcha, in its forward-axis form).
